audit_findings.title: AMS closing would obsolete both the earnings numerator and financing perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: £659 million equity value, £715 million enterprise value, and up to $3.0 billion of bridge financing
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing adds AMS owner earnings while changing interest expense, acquisition costs, debt and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Future acquisitions could result in additional debt and other liabilities, and increased interest expense, restructuring charges and amortization expense related to intangible assets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a prospective perimeter change, not an error in the as-filed valuation. The transaction is large enough to require a complete combined-company valuation, but its net effect is presently indeterminate because target owner earnings, permanent financing, fees and integration costs are not supplied.
audit_findings.action: At closing, obtain the final consideration, acquired cash and debt, permanent financing, fees, purchase accounting, integration costs and normalized AMS owner earnings, then rerun all scenarios on the combined perimeter.

audit_findings.title: A material net-investment-hedge liability may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $119.332 million, or $2.01 per diluted share; 3.5% of $3.405 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net economic derivative liability not offset elsewhere must reduce the equity bridge; related interest or settlement effects may also enter owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of November 29, 2025 , the combined fair value of the swaps wa s a liability of $ 113,144 and was included in other liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $119.332 million liability, but it does not demonstrate that the whole amount is an omitted standalone claim: the swaps hedge translated foreign investments, and offsetting translation economics or derivative cash flows may already be reflected. A full deduction would reduce base value from $57.23 to about $55.22 per share, narrowing the premium to the $53.89 price from $3.34 to $1.33 per share. The possible effect is meaningful, but the record cannot establish the required net adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every latest derivative asset and liability, accumulated translation effects, forecast foreign earnings, interest income and expected settlements; rerun after deducting only the net economic liability not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition holdback principal is a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.494 million remaining, or $0.38 per diluted share; 0.66% of $3.405 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unmodeled holdback principal reduces the equity bridge because its payment is not an owner-earnings expense apart from interest accretion.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the holdback liability related to the acquisition of GEM and Medifill, based on a discounted cash flow model, was $ 33,578 as of November 29, 2025 .
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing shows that $11.596 million was paid and $22.494 million remains. Deducting the entire remaining liability would reduce base value from $57.23 to about $56.85 per share and the $40.06 buy-below level to about $39.80. That scale does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the remaining payment schedule and whether projected owner earnings explicitly include the payments; otherwise deduct $22.494 million in a bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: The Rouse settlement becomes an omitted cash claim if its loss was added back
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.8 million accrued, $26.3 million after tax, with gross settlement capped at $75.0 million; the cap equals $1.26 per diluted share and 2.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If the litigation charge was removed from owner earnings, the unpaid settlement liability must reduce the bridge, net only of a recognized or demonstrably collectible insurance recovery.
audit_findings.evidence: At that mediation session, the Company and the plaintiffs agreed in principle to settle this matter for up to $75.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish whether the $34.8 million charge was added back in the owner-earnings worksheet, so an error is not demonstrated. Even deducting the full $75.0 million gross cap would reduce base value from $57.23 to about $55.97 per share, still above the $53.89 market price, and would reduce the buy-below level by about $0.88. On the filed maximum, this does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the charge through the FY2025 owner-earnings worksheet, confirm the latest accrual and claims estimate, and rerun with any added-back amount offset by the unpaid liability less only recorded or demonstrably collectible insurance.

audit_findings.title: Project ONE costs are not safely excludable as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.237 million of FY2025 costs, $5.440 million in the first six months of 2026, and $35 million to $55 million of computed remaining expenditures against the filed $300 million to $320 million estimate and $265 million spent
audit_findings.mechanism: Improper expense add-backs overstate anchor owner earnings, while any omitted maintenance or implementation capital spending also overstates owner earnings and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2026 and beyond, we will continue implementation in Brazil and Asia Pacific.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that Project ONE spending continues into 2026 and beyond, but the supplied valuation does not show whether these costs were removed from the $229.7 million anchor or whether capitalized amounts were already captured through capital expenditure deductions. The recurring burden may affect value, but its materiality cannot be established without the worksheet and the expense-versus-capital split.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every historical Project ONE adjustment, separate expensed costs from capital expenditures already deducted, retain recurring implementation and maintenance burdens, and rerun the anchor and scenarios if any were excluded.

audit_findings.title: The Sekisui-Fuller stake may be counted in both earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum potential duplicated bridge amount of $53.9 million, or $0.91 per diluted share and 1.6% of base equity value; FY2025 equity-method income was $3.784 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Including Sekisui-Fuller earnings in owner earnings while separately adding its stake value duplicates value between the earnings numerator and equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The income from equity method investments relates to our 50 percent ownership of the Sekisui-Fuller joint venture in Japan.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that consolidated income contains Sekisui-Fuller equity-method earnings, but the record does not identify the assets composing the $53.9 million stakes bridge, so duplication is not demonstrated. Even treating the entire $53.9 million bridge amount as duplicated would reduce base value only from $57.23 to about $56.32 per share and the buy-below level by about $0.63, without changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: List every asset in stakes_net and trace equity-method income through each OE year; if Sekisui-Fuller is included in both places, rerun using either distributable earnings or separately added stake value, but not both.
